como.eyebrow: Information that gains value over time
como.title: Owners have a lot to tell.
como.intro: Duraverso brings together usage experiences with products that work well, needed repairs or stopped working.

sections.title: Find the right model
sections.text: Browsing is public: search by brand and model or by barcode. Before contributing, you’ll need to confirm the variant, including its voltage.

sections.title: Satisfaction and durability are different
sections.text: The Community Score reflects satisfaction, from 1 to 5 stars. The performance and repair history describes experiences over time. A high score doesn’t guarantee a long lifespan.

sections.title: When does an average appear?
sections.text: With fewer than 20 eligible ratings from different owners per variant, only individual reports and the number of contributions are shown. From that threshold on, the average is labeled preliminary — and that number doesn’t guarantee statistical representativeness.

sections.title: An experience can change
sections.text: Each person will have one active rating per model. Updates replace the previous vote. Repairs add events to the history, not new votes.

sections.title: Working fine matters too
sections.text: You don’t need a complaint to take part: an owner can report that the product is still working. If they don’t come back, we won’t assume the product is still in use — the date of the last confirmation stays visible.

sections.title: Transparency about the pilot
sections.text: This preview lets you explore candidate home appliance models and try the search. Login, publishing experiences and administrative review are not active yet. There are no fictitious reviews and no collection of receipts.

regras.title: An honest story is worth more.
regras.intro: These are the rules planned for the pilot.

sections.title: Share your experience
sections.text: Contribute about a product you use or have used, identify the model correctly, and keep in mind that other people may have different experiences.

sections.title: Describe what happened
sections.text: Report the symptom and the repair separately — for example, “It stopped spinning” and “The control board had to be replaced”. If you don’t know the cause, say so.

sections.title: Protect personal data
sections.text: Don’t include phone numbers, addresses, documents, serial numbers or other people’s data. Photos and receipts are not part of the first phase.

sections.title: Equal review criteria
sections.text: Positive and negative reports follow the same criteria. Review may ask for corrections but won’t change your rating or opinion. Advertising, personal attacks, copied reports and vote manipulation aren’t accepted.

sections.title: Right to correct and appeal
sections.text: You’ll be able to update or withdraw a contribution. Decisions not to publish will give the reason and let you ask for reconsideration.

sections.title: A declared report isn’t proof
sections.text: Signing in with Google will give access to your account, but it doesn’t prove ownership, repairs or a person’s unique identity. Manual review doesn’t turn a report into documentary evidence.

privacidade.title: Clarity about your data.
privacidade.intro: In effect since 11/07/2026. The public preview only lets you browse the catalog, with no accounts. The closed, invitation-only pilot has Google sign-in and report submission. Controller: Paulo Gomes. Contact: netface@gmail.com.

sections.title: Who looks after your data
sections.text: Duraverso is a personal project maintained by Paulo Gomes, who is responsible for the data processed here. Questions, requests and complaints about personal data: netface@gmail.com.

sections.title: What we keep in the pilot
sections.text: When you sign in with Google, we keep only the identifier Google assigns to your account and a public nickname, which starts as “Proprietário” (Owner) and can be changed. We don’t keep your email, your photo or access to your Google account. In reports and repairs, we keep what you enter: model and version, start of use, how you acquired it, the appliance’s condition, repairs, costs, ratings and comments.

sections.title: What we use it for
sections.text: To review and publish your reports, show your history in your account, compute the public counts and averages, and protect the site against abuse. We don’t sell or share data for advertising, and the site has no ads or visitor analytics tools.

sections.title: What becomes public
sections.text: Only your nickname and approved reports and repairs. Your Google identifier and account data never appear. Every contribution is reviewed manually before publication.

sections.title: Service providers
sections.text: Vercel (hosting), Neon (database) and Google (sign-in). These services process data on servers outside Brazil, mainly in the United States. Hosting may create technical access logs (IP address, time and page).

sections.title: Search and camera
sections.text: What you search for appears in the page address and may stay in your browser history; avoid personal information in searches. The camera only opens when you tap “Open camera”; the code is read on your device and no image is sent to Duraverso.

sections.title: Session cookie
sections.text: In the pilot, signing in with Google creates a session cookie that lasts up to 24 hours. Signing out of all devices invalidates open sessions. There are no advertising or tracking cookies.

sections.title: How long we keep it
sections.text: Your account, reports and repairs are kept until you ask for deletion; withdrawn reports and repairs stop appearing but stay linked to the account until that request. Deletion requests are handled within 15 days. The record of moderation decisions (reason, moderator and date) is kept for up to 1 year after deletion, to answer disputes. Technical access logs follow Vercel’s retention periods.

sections.title: Your rights and deletion
sections.text: In your account you can change your nickname, update or withdraw reports and repairs, and end sessions. To access your data, correct something not available in the account, or delete the account and everything linked to it, write to netface@gmail.com. To confirm the account is yours without asking for documents, we’ll ask you to temporarily change your public nickname to a code we send you.
